import pandas as pd

reps = pd.DataFrame({"rep": ["Ana", "Ben", "Cho", "Dev", "Eli"], "sales": [9800, 10000, 24999, 51000, 30250]})
tiers = pd.DataFrame({"min_sales": [0, 10000, 25000, 50000], "rate": [0.00, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06]})

out = pd.merge_asof(reps.sort_values("sales"), tiers, left_on="sales", right_on="min_sales").set_index("rep").loc[reps["rep"]]
for rep, row in out.iterrows():
    print(f"{rep}: {row['rate']}")

guided.title: VLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH
guided.prompt: Interview question: `When would you use XLOOKUP instead of VLOOKUP, and what is INDEX/MATCH for?` Give a three-part answer (what, why, risk) in about 100 words.
guided.solution:
What: all three return a value from a table row found by a key. `VLOOKUP` searches the first column and returns a column by its number; `XLOOKUP` takes separate lookup and return ranges; `INDEX`/`MATCH` combines a position finder with a range picker.

Why: I prefer `XLOOKUP` (or `INDEX`/`MATCH` in versions without it) because it does not break when columns are inserted, can look left, and defaults to an exact match; `VLOOKUP` hard-codes a column number and defaults to approximate match when the last argument is omitted.

Risk: a missing key returns `#N/A`, so give `XLOOKUP` a not-found text and count misses with `COUNTIF` or `ISNA`; and approximate match on an unsorted first column returns wrong results.
hints: Which one breaks when a column is inserted?
What does a missing key return?
rubric: Says what each does in one line.
Gives the column-number and look-left reasons.
Names the missing-key or approximate-match risk.

independent.title: Why do the totals disagree
independent.prompt: A manager says: `The matrix by country adds up to less than the total revenue card`. List five causes in the order you would check them, what you look at for each, and the fix for the most likely one.
independent.solution:
Order of checks: (1) orphan keys: sales whose `customer_id` is missing from `Customers` show under a blank country; check with an anti-join or the blank row in the matrix and fix the dimension or the source keys. (2) A relationship that is inactive or filters the wrong way, so the country filter does not reach `Sales`; check Model view. (3) A measure that uses `ALL` or a fixed filter and ignores the country on the rows. (4) A visual-level or page filter that removes rows from the matrix but not the card. (5) A partial or stale refresh, or a date table that does not cover all dates.

The most likely fix is for orphans: correct or add the missing customers, refresh, and reconcile so that the sum of countries (including the blank group, which should disappear) equals the card total.
rubric: Lists orphan keys, relationships, measure filters, visual filters and refresh or date coverage.
Says how to check each one.
Gives a fix for orphans and a reconciliation check.

environment.note: Excel, Power BI Desktop (Windows only) and DAX have no runtime in this course's browser. The formulas and DAX are shown as text, and every number in the lesson and in the model answers is reproduced with pandas, which runs in the browser. Function names are those of current Excel (XLOOKUP needs a recent version) and Power BI. The graded exercises are pandas replicas; the written exercises are model answers marked against a rubric.

checks.question: `VLOOKUP(x, table, 2)` with the last argument omitted does what?
options: An approximate match that needs a sorted first column
checks.explanation: Omitting the last argument is the same as TRUE, which is approximate match on sorted data. Use FALSE for exact.

checks.question: What does `ALL(Customers)` do inside `CALCULATE` for a percent-of-total measure?
options: Removes filters from Customers so the denominator is the overall total
Adds all customers to the visual
checks.explanation: The denominator must ignore the country on the rows, which ALL achieves; the numerator keeps the filter.

checks.question: Why does a PivotTable show Count instead of Sum for a column?
options: The column contains text or blanks
checks.explanation: Excel defaults to Count when a values field has non-numeric entries; clean the data or switch the aggregation.

checks.question: A measure is different from a calculated column because:
options: It is computed at report time for the current filters
It is stored for every row
checks.explanation: Measures respond to filter context when the visual is drawn; calculated columns are fixed at refresh.

checks.question: A rep has sales of 24,999 and tiers start at 0, 10,000, 25,000, 50,000. Which tier applies with approximate match?
checks.explanation: Approximate match returns the largest minimum not above the value: 10,000 is, 25,000 is not.
